    Kraken Launches Pre-IPO Perpetual Futures for OpenAI and Anthropic

    Kraken launches pre-IPO perpetual futures for OpenAI and Anthropic with up to 5x leverage. No shares, no IPO needed. U.S. traders excluded.
    By Trader EdgeSeptember 7, 20263 Mins Read
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 3:32
    Instaread

    TLDR

    • Kraken has launched cash-settled perpetual futures contracts for OpenAI and Anthropic, allowing traders to go long or short before either company goes public.
    • Both contracts offer up to 5x leverage with no expiry date and support multi-collateral margin.
    • Pricing uses Kraken’s own synthetic index since neither company has publicly traded shares.
    • The contracts are unavailable in the U.S., European Economic Area, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
    • If either company completes an IPO, Kraken plans to switch pricing to a tokenized equity-based index.

    Kraken has launched perpetual futures contracts tied to the private-market valuations of OpenAI and Anthropic. The products let eligible traders take leveraged positions on both AI companies before either completes a public stock listing.

    The contracts are cash-settled and have no expiration date. Traders can go long or short, and both products support multi-collateral margin through Kraken’s flex account system.

    How the Contracts Work

    The OpenAI contract trades under the symbol PF_OPENAIXUSD. The Anthropic contract trades as PF_ANTHROPICXUSD. Kraken confirmed support for both on September 6, 2026.

    Holding either contract does not give traders any shares, voting rights, dividends, or ownership in either company. The contracts simply track traders’ expectations of each company’s value.

    Maximum leverage is 5x at the base tier. This requires an initial margin of 20% of the position’s value. Maintenance margin sits at 10%, and leverage steps down for larger positions.

    Funding payments are settled every hour. Kraken describes these funding costs as low during the pre-IPO period due to how tightly the mark price is managed.

    Traders can lose all of their margin. Kraken also warns that losses can exceed the initial deposit depending on account conditions.

    How Kraken Prices Private Companies

    Because neither OpenAI nor Anthropic has publicly traded shares, Kraken built its own pricing tool called the Kraken PreMarket Synthetic index.

    The index derives its value from activity within the perpetual market itself rather than from an external stock price. Kraken applies exponential smoothing to reduce the effect of short-term price spikes.

    The mark price is clamped within a 0.25% band around the synthetic index at all times. This is designed to limit sudden liquidations in a market that may have low liquidity.

    The protection does not remove valuation risk. If traders collectively misjudge a company’s value, the synthetic index can reflect that error with no outside price to correct it.

    Anthropic-linked futures on other platforms have previously dropped as much as 9% following new exchange listings, showing how sharply these contracts can move.

    Geographic Restrictions and Regulatory Context

    The contracts are not available to customers in the U.S., European Economic Area, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand. In the United Kingdom, access is limited to professional clients only.

    Payward Digital Solutions offers the products from Bermuda under a license from the Bermuda Monetary Authority.

    Other exchanges, including Coinbase and Hyperliquid, have also listed private-company perpetuals for eligible non-U.S. users.

    If OpenAI or Anthropic completes an IPO, Kraken plans to replace the synthetic index with pricing tied to its xStocks tokenized equity products. If no IPO occurs, Kraken may delist and settle the contracts.

    Bitcoin (BTC) Price: BTC Dips but Institutions Keep Buying — Here’s What Traders Are Watching Now

    Bitcoin (BTC) price: BTC falls below $80K as Fed rate hike bets rise to 60%, oil hits $97, and a $320M Liquid Network exploit rattles markets.
    By Trader EdgeSeptember 7, 20263 Mins Read

    TLDR

    • Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 after strong U.S. jobs data boosted Fed rate hike bets to 60%
    • BTC hit a three-month high of $82,178 last Thursday before pulling back
    • Brent crude hit $97/barrel due to U.S.-Iran tensions, adding pressure on risk assets
    • Bitcoin’s Liquid Network suffered a $320 million exploit, draining ~4,000 BTC
    • U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $1 billion in net inflows last week, with $175 million on September 4 alone

    Bitcoin is trading around $79,724 on Monday, down about 0.3% on the day. The drop comes after a strong U.S. jobs report on Friday rattled risk assets across the board.

    U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August — nearly triple what economists expected. The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%.

    That data pushed markets to price a roughly 60% probability of a Fed rate hike at the September 15–16 meeting, up from 49% before the report, according to CME FedWatch.

    Bitcoin had briefly climbed above $82,000 last week, touching a three-month high of $82,178 on Thursday. That rally stalled after the jobs numbers came in.

    Higher interest rates tend to weigh on Bitcoin. They raise the cost of holding non-yielding assets and tighten financial conditions more broadly.

    Oil Prices Add to the Pressure

    Oil prices are also playing a role. Brent crude climbed to around $97 a barrel Monday as U.S.-Iran military tensions raised fears of supply disruptions.

    The U.S. military struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday after Iran targeted U.S. Navy vessels with ballistic missiles. That pushed oil higher and added another layer of uncertainty for investors.

    Analysts are now watching Thursday’s U.S. producer price data and Friday’s consumer price index for more clues on the Fed’s next move.

    $320 Million Exploit Hits Bitcoin’s Liquid Network

    Bitcoin’s Liquid Network, a settlement layer used by exchanges, halted new transactions after approximately $320 million in bitcoin was drained from its federation wallet.

    Around 4,000 of the roughly 4,200 BTC held in the wallet were taken. The withdrawals were carried out through SideSwap, a platform authorized to operate on the network.

    Those responsible described themselves as “purported white-hat hackers,” though their identities and intentions remain unclear. Exchanges have suspended LBTC deposits and withdrawals while the investigation continues.

    Analyst Ted Pillows posted on X that BTC is hovering near the $80,000 level and flagged the weekly close as the key metric to watch. He noted that Bitcoin is close to the 50-week moving average, and a weekly close above it would make a strong case that Bitcoin has found its bottom.

    Institutional Demand Holds Firm

    Despite the pressure, institutional demand has stayed steady. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $175 million in net inflows on September 4, their third straight positive session.

    BlackRock’s IBIT led with $117 million in inflows, followed by Fidelity with $57.22 million. Total ETF inflows for the week reached approximately $1 billion.

    Kalshi traders are pricing a 77% probability that Bitcoin crosses $85,000 before October 2. That would require a gain of roughly 6.3% from current levels.

    Bitcoin’s four-hour RSI sits at 55.20, reflecting neutral momentum. The MACD histogram is showing a slight bearish reading at -66.35, though both MACD lines remain above zero.

    The key support level to hold is $79,500. A move above $82,000 would be the next step toward a push for $85,000.
